new_findings_r2.title: reconnect() collapses a host 'uncertain' attach disposition into 'attached' instead of passing it through
new_findings_r2.description: `return this.settled(tokened, handle.disposition === "terminal" ? "terminal" : "attached", ...)` maps any non-'terminal' host disposition to 'attached', silently absorbing 'uncertain' (which the wire protocol and host-launch-supervisor.ts's attachLive() legitimately return when a restarted host's runner.inspect() cannot determine guest state, host-launch-supervisor.ts:81). The sibling primary path in the same file, open() at line 62, passes `handle.disposition` straight through unmodified, so this is an inconsistency introduced by the fix rather than a pre-existing pattern. Currently behaviorally inert: the only production caller, IsolatedFactoryTrustedRunner.dispatch() equivalent at src/factory/runner/attempt-runtime.ts:785, does `(await this.runtime.open(...)).wait()` and never reads `.disposition`, and reconnect()'s own wait() closure (lines 97-102) independently produces a typed launch_uncertain rejection when the host has nothing to report, regardless of the mislabeled disposition field. Still worth matching open()'s pass-through for correctness and for any future consumer (logging, monitoring, a UI) that reads `.disposition`.
new_findings_r2.recommendation: Change line 97 to pass `handle.disposition` through unmodified (matching line 62's pattern), or explicitly map both 'terminal' and 'uncertain' rather than defaulting everything else to 'attached'.

new_findings_r2.title: The 'supervisor also restarted, host holds nothing' sub-case of the reconnect fix has no dedicated end-to-end test; the green coverage gate cannot certify it because this repo's lcov is line-only, not branch-aware
new_findings_r2.description: The team lead's brief asked to confirm the remote runtime 'stays uncertain (typed, not guessed) when the supervisor also restarted.' By code tracing this is correct: if a second, independent supervisor has restarted (live map empty) and its runner reports the guest as fully gone or unknown, host-launch-supervisor.ts's attachLive() returns disposition 'terminal' or 'uncertain' without registering anything in `live`; back in reconnect(), the wait() closure's `awaitResult()` call then hits supervisor.result() finding no `live` entry, which throws FactoryAttemptRuntimeError('launch_uncertain', 'This host is not running that attempt.'); reconnect()'s catch on line 101 re-wraps that as the same typed launch_uncertain error. That reasoning is sound, but no test in this diff or the pre-existing suite drives this exact combination (gateway restarted AND supervisor restarted AND host holds nothing) through FactoryRemoteAttemptRuntime.open()/reconnect() end to end; the pre-existing 'restarted supervisor reattaches' test (host-launch-transport.integration.test.ts:167-224) calls `client.attach(intent)` directly, bypassing the gateway's reconnect() and its wait()/result() sequencing entirely. Separately, scripts/merge-lcov.ts's own header comment states 'Bun 1.3.x emits no BRDA records, so branch data is intentionally not handled' -- this repo's coverage gates are line-only. Reading the merged lcov for the new reconnect() method shows every line, including the untested catch branches at lines 91-95 and 100-101, reporting a nonzero DA count even in a coverage run isolated to just the one new happy-path test (verified by running `bun test -t "gateway that restarts mid-launch"` alone and diffing the resulting lcov against the full-suite lcov: the two are byte-for-byte identical on those lines). That is consistent with V8/Bun collapsing adjacent try/catch ranges in small async functions rather than tracking the catch body's true entry independently, so a 100% patch-coverage gate on this file does not by itself prove the uncertain-outcome branch was exercised by any test.
new_findings_r2.recommendation: Add a unit or integration case that forces transport.attach() to return disposition 'terminal' or 'uncertain' with no durable terminal result recorded (e.g. inject a fake FactoryHostLaunchTransport whose attach() returns disposition:'terminal' and whose result() throws, mirroring the shape host-launch-client.ts actually returns after a double restart), and assert reconnect()'s resulting .wait() rejects with a FactoryAttemptRuntimeError code 'launch_uncertain' rather than resolving to a guessed result. This directly proves the sentence in the commit message and lessons.md rather than leaving it to composition-by-inspection.
